newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon public finances at turning point - B.Audi.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon public finances at turning point - B.Audi.

text.p: Lebanon's public debt grew 43.7 percent in real terms in 1996 to 13,358.2 billion Lebanese pounds and the country's finances are at a crucial turning point, Banque Audi said in its latest economic report on Monday.
The "utmost rigour and discipline" was needed to contain the public debt within acceptable limits," the bank said in its report for the final quarter of 1996.

"Lebanon is at a very important turning point in the recovery of its public finances which requires the utmost rigour and discipline in the rationalisation of its budgetary choices, the optimisation of its policy on taxes, the limitation of evasion and waste and the mobilisation of domestic and foreign resources for investment," it said.
Despite government efforts to date "far more drastic measures should be envisaged in order to limit losses and preserve the macro-economic achievements of the past four years," the bank added.
It quoted central bank figures as indicating that Lebanon's external debt rose 37 percent in 1996 to $1.769 billion from 1.291 billion.

Banque Audi called for "serious respect for budgetary rigour and discipline over the next few months" following parliament's approval last month of a 1997 budget law with a 36.3 percent deficit revenue to expenditure.

"The government must...recover the lasting confidence of international investors, whose contribution to development in Lebanon is indispensable, revive the economy to avoid any further erosion of the middle class, and face up to the annual growth of the working population, while coping with imbalances," the bank said.

It said the government could achieve a current budget surplus by the year 2,000 and a global surplus by 2002 if the economy grew by six percent a year and it increased tax levying by one percent a year in relation to GNP and reduced the annual debt service rate by two percent a year and froze the wage bill.
